column6: Boaz, a near kinsman, paid the price to redeem what was lost and took Ruth, a Gentile, as his bride. Christ became our kinsman, taking our nature, to redeem us.
Hannah's song ends: the LORD shall give strength unto his king and exalt the horn of his anointed (his Messiah). Zacharias sings that God has raised up "an horn of salvation" in David's house.
The shepherd from Bethlehem faced the enemy his people feared, alone, and won the victory they all shared. Traditionally a picture of Christ's victory over Satan.

column2: David's son, a throne for ever
column6: God promised David a son whose kingdom and throne would last for ever, and "I will be his father, and he shall be my son". Fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David and Son of God.
The queen of Sheba came from far away to hear Solomon's wisdom. Jesus said, "a greater than Solomon is here", in whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom.

column2: I know that my redeemer liveth
column6: In his suffering Job is sure his Redeemer lives and will stand on the earth at the last, and that he will see God in his flesh. Fulfilled in the risen Christ and the resurrection of believers.
Joshua (the same name as Jesus) led the people into the promised rest that Moses could not. Hebrews points beyond him to the rest that Jesus gives.

column2: The captain of the LORD's host
column6: Before Jericho, Joshua met a man with a drawn sword, the captain of the LORD's host, and worshipped him on holy ground. Traditionally an appearance of Christ, the captain of our salvation.
I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart. Hebrews calls Jesus the merciful and faithful high priest.

column2: The first promise of the gospel
column6: The woman's offspring would crush the serpent's head, though bruised himself. Christ, born of a woman, defeated Satan by his death on the cross.
God himself covered Adam and Eve's shame with skins, which cost a death. So Christ's righteousness, won by his death, covers the sinner.

column2: Adam, a figure of him to come
column6: Paul calls Adam "the figure of him that was to come". Through the first Adam came sin and death; through Christ, the last Adam, righteousness and life.
The first marriage, the bride taken from the man's side, is "a great mystery" that Paul says speaks of Christ and the church.
Abel brought a lamb from his flock and God accepted it. Christ is the Lamb of God, whose blood "speaketh better things than that of Abel".
Noah's family were brought safely through the judgement of the flood inside the ark, with its one door. So believers are saved from judgement in Christ.
God promised that in Abraham all the families of the earth would be blessed. Paul calls this the gospel preached beforehand, fulfilled as the nations are blessed in Christ.
King of righteousness and of peace, bringing bread and wine, priest of the most high God with no recorded beginning or end. Hebrews says Christ is a priest for ever in his order.
A father offers his beloved only son on Moriah; the son carries the wood up the hill; "God will provide himself a lamb"; a ram dies in his place. A picture of the Father giving his Son.
In thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed. Paul points out that it says seed, not seeds: "which is Christ".
Jacob saw a ladder joining earth to heaven, with angels going up and down. Jesus said this is the Son of Man: he is the way between heaven and earth.

column2: Joseph, rejected and then the saviour
column6: Loved by his father, hated and sold by his brothers for silver, Joseph was raised to the right hand of the king and saved the brothers who betrayed him. A picture of Christ.
The ruler's sceptre would not leave Judah "until Shiloh come", and the peoples would gather to him. Christ came from Judah, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, King for ever.
Moses was first refused by his own people ("Who made thee a prince?") and then sent by God to deliver them. Stephen says Christ was rejected in the same way, and is the greater deliverer.
A lamb without blemish was killed and its blood put on the door, and death passed over that house; not a bone of it was to be broken. "Christ our passover is sacrificed for us."
God fed Israel in the wilderness with bread from heaven. Jesus said: "I am the bread of life... the living bread which came down from heaven."
Water flowed from the rock when it was struck, and the people drank. Paul says plainly, "that Rock was Christ"; struck once, he gives living water.
The tabernacle was God's tent among Israel, filled with his glory. "The Word was made flesh, and dwelt (tabernacled) among us, and we beheld his glory."
On the lid of the ark the blood of atonement was sprinkled and God met with his people. Paul calls Christ the propitiation, the same word as mercy seat.
The veil shut the way into God's presence. When Christ died it was torn from top to bottom; Hebrews says the veil is his flesh, the new and living way.
Aaron bore the names of the tribes on his heart before God and bore the iniquity of their gifts. Christ is the great high priest who lives for ever to intercede for his people.
A male without blemish, wholly given up to God, a sweet savour, accepted for the one who brought it. Christ "hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour".

column2: The sin offering, burned outside the camp
column6: The sinner laid his hand on the animal, which died for his sin, and its body was burned outside the camp. So Jesus, made sin for us, "suffered without the gate".
God gave the blood on the altar to make atonement for souls. "Without shedding of blood is no remission": the blood of Christ cleanses from all sin.

column2: The Day of Atonement and the scapegoat
column6: Once a year the high priest took blood into the holiest place, and a goat carried the people's sins away into the wilderness. Christ entered heaven once for all with his own blood and took away sin.
The first sheaf of the harvest was waved before the LORD the day after the sabbath. Christ rose on that day, "the firstfruits of them that slept", the pledge of the harvest to come.
A heifer without spot, slain outside the camp, whose ashes cleansed the unclean. Hebrews: how much more shall the blood of Christ purge your conscience.
Whoever looked at the serpent lifted up on the pole lived. Jesus: "As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up."
Balaam saw a Star come out of Jacob and a Sceptre rise out of Israel. Christ is "the bright and morning star", the King whose star the wise men followed.
The one who fled to a city of refuge was safe from the avenger, until the high priest died. Believers "have fled for refuge" to Christ, the high priest who lives for ever.
God promised to raise up a prophet like Moses, with his words in his mouth, whom all must hear. Peter and Stephen preached that this prophet is Jesus.
He that is hanged is accursed of God. Paul quotes this of the cross: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.
The bread of the presence lay always before the LORD, and the golden lampstand gave the only light in the holy place. Jesus: "I am the bread of life" and "I am the light of the world."
At the bronze altar, outside the tent, every sacrifice was offered; no one came to God without passing it. "We have an altar": the cross where Christ offered himself once for all.
Every day a lamb was offered in the morning and another in the evening, without end. Christ, the Lamb of God, offered one sacrifice for sins for ever.
Incense burned before the veil morning and evening, a picture of prayer rising to God. Christ "ever liveth to make intercession" for his people.
A sacrifice shared with God and the worshipper in fellowship. Christ "is our peace", having made peace through the blood of his cross.
One bird was killed over running water, and the living bird, dipped in its blood, was let go: the leper was clean. A picture of Christ's death and resurrection cleansing the sinner.

On the Day of Atonement the trumpet sounded liberty throughout the land; debts were cancelled and the captive went home. Jesus came "to preach deliverance to the captives... the acceptable year of the Lord".
A dead rod brought forth buds, blossoms and almonds overnight, showing whom God had chosen as priest. Traditionally a picture of Christ, the chosen priest, raised to life.

column2: The nations against the LORD's anointed
column6: The kings of the earth set themselves against the LORD and his anointed. The apostles prayed that this was fulfilled when Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles and Israel gathered against Jesus.
Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee. The New Testament applies this to Jesus, declared the Son of God with power by his resurrection, who will rule the nations.

column2: Out of the mouth of babes
column6: When the children in the temple cried "Hosanna to the Son of David", Jesus answered with this verse: God has perfected praise out of the mouths of babes.

column2: Crowned with glory, all things under his feet
column6: Man made a little lower than the angels and crowned with glory. Hebrews: "we see Jesus", who for the suffering of death is crowned with glory, with all things put under him.
Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; neither wilt thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption. Peter and Paul preach that David spoke of the resurrection of Christ.

column2: My God, why hast thou forsaken me?
column6: Jesus cried the first words of this psalm from the cross. The whole psalm, written a thousand years before, describes the crucifixion.
Despised by the people, they shake the head: "He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him." The rulers used almost these words as they mocked Jesus on the cross.

column2: They pierced my hands and my feet
column6: Poured out like water, bones out of joint, tongue cleaving to the jaws, hands and feet pierced. A picture of crucifixion, a death not yet known when it was written.
They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture. The soldiers did exactly this at the foot of the cross.

column2: All the ends of the world shall turn
column6: The psalm of the cross ends in triumph: all the nations turn to the LORD, and his righteousness is declared, "that he hath done this". Fulfilled as the gospel goes to all nations.

column2: I will declare thy name unto my brethren
column6: After the suffering, praise. Hebrews puts these words in Christ's mouth: he is not ashamed to call his people brethren.
The LORD is the shepherd of his people. Jesus says, "I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep."
Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and the King of glory shall come in. Traditionally sung of Christ's ascension; Paul calls Jesus "the Lord of glory".

column2: Into thine hand I commit my spirit
column6: Jesus' last words on the cross were these: "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit."

column2: Not one of his bones broken
column6: The soldiers broke the legs of the two thieves but not of Jesus, who was already dead, "that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken."

column2: False witnesses and hatred without a cause
column6: False witnesses rose up; "they hated me without a cause". Jesus said this word was fulfilled in him.

column2: Lo, I come to do thy will
column6: Sacrifices God did not desire, but "Lo, I come... I delight to do thy will". Hebrews says Christ spoke these words coming into the world, and by that will we are sanctified through his body offered once for all.
Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me. Jesus quoted this of Judas at the Last Supper.

column2: Thy throne, O God, is for ever
column6: The royal psalm calls the king God, anointed with the oil of gladness above his fellows. Hebrews says God says this "unto the Son".

column2: Let all the gods worship him
column6: Worship him, all ye gods. Hebrews applies this to the Son: "when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him."
Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive: thou hast received gifts for men. Paul applies it to Christ's ascension and the gifts he gives his church.
A stranger to his brothers, eaten up with zeal for God's house, bearing the reproaches meant for God. The disciples remembered this when Jesus cleared the temple.
In my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. On the cross Jesus said "I thirst", and was given vinegar.
Peter quoted these verses of Judas, who betrayed Jesus, when the apostles chose another to take his place.
Kings shall bring presents and all nations shall serve him and call him blessed. The wise men from the east brought gifts to the infant Christ.
I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old. Matthew says Jesus taught in parables to fulfil this.
God swore that David's seed would endure for ever and his throne as the days of heaven; "I will make him my firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth". Fulfilled in Christ.
The heavens will perish, "but thou art the same, and thy years shall have no end". Hebrews says this is spoken to the Son, the Creator.

column2: Sit thou at my right hand
column6: The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand. Jesus asked how David's son could be David's Lord; the apostles preach him seated at God's right hand. The verse the New Testament quotes most.
Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek. Hebrews builds on this oath: Christ, King and Priest, lives for ever to make intercession.
The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. Jesus applied it to himself, and Peter preached it of his rejection and resurrection.
The crowds sang this psalm as Jesus rode into Jerusalem: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord."

column2: Of the fruit of thy body upon thy throne
column6: God swore to David that of the fruit of his body he would set one on his throne. Peter says David, a prophet, knew this and spoke of the resurrection of Christ.
Wisdom was with the LORD before the world, beside him as he made all things, his daily delight. Traditionally read of Christ, "the wisdom of God", by whom all things were made.
Isaiah saw the Lord on his throne, high and lifted up, and heard "Holy, holy, holy". John says, "These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him": of Jesus.
A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel, God with us. Matthew says Jesus' birth of the virgin Mary fulfilled it.
The LORD would be a sanctuary, but a stone of stumbling to both houses of Israel. Paul and Peter say Christ is this stone, a refuge to those who trust and a stumbling block to those who refuse.
The people of Galilee of the nations, who walked in darkness, have seen a great light. Matthew says this was fulfilled when Jesus began to preach there.

column2: Unto us a child is born
column6: A child born, a son given, called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace, on David's throne for ever. Fulfilled in Jesus.

column2: A rod out of the stem of Jesse
column6: A shoot from the stump of Jesse (David's father), with the Spirit of the LORD resting on him, judging in righteousness; the Gentiles shall seek him. Fulfilled in Christ, the root and offspring of David.
The key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut. Jesus applies it to himself: "he that hath the key of David".
He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces. Fulfilled in Christ's resurrection and, in full, at his return.
A tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation; "he that believeth shall not make haste". Paul and Peter say this stone is Christ.

column2: The blind see, the lame leap
column6: Your God will come... Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened. When John the Baptist asked if Jesus was the one, Jesus pointed to these very signs.

column2: Prepare ye the way of the LORD
column6: A voice in the wilderness prepares the way of the LORD, and all flesh shall see his glory. John the Baptist was that voice; the LORD whose way he prepared was Jesus.

column2: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd
column6: Behold your God! He comes with strength, and feeds his flock like a shepherd, carrying the lambs. Jesus, the good shepherd, is God come to his people.

column2: My servant, in whom my soul delighteth
column6: God's chosen servant, with his Spirit on him, gentle (he will not break a bruised reed), bringing justice to the Gentiles. Matthew says this is Jesus.

The servant is a covenant for the people and a light to the nations, opening blind eyes, God's salvation to the end of the earth. Simeon held the baby Jesus and called him "a light to lighten the Gentiles".
Unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. Paul applies these words, spoken by the LORD, to Jesus: every knee shall bow at his name.

column2: I gave my back to the smiters
column6: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting. So Jesus was beaten, spat on and scourged.
The servant will be lifted up very high, after his face was marred more than any man's, and he shall sprinkle many nations. The start of Isaiah's song of the suffering servant.
Who has believed? He grew up with no beauty to draw us; despised and rejected, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. So Jesus was rejected by his own.
He was wounded for our transgressions... with his stripes we are healed... the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all. The heart of the gospel: Christ died in our place.

column2: As a lamb to the slaughter
column6: Oppressed and afflicted, he opened not his mouth, led as a lamb to the slaughter, cut off for the transgression of my people. Philip began at this scripture and preached Jesus.

column2: With the rich in his death
column6: He made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence. Jesus died between thieves and was buried in a rich man's tomb.

An offering for sin, yet he shall prolong his days and see his seed; he bore the sin of many, was numbered with the transgressors, and made intercession for them. His death, resurrection and prayer for us.
I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. Paul preached that God gave these by raising Jesus from the dead, no more to return to corruption.

column2: The Redeemer shall come to Zion
column6: The Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob. Paul quotes it of Christ: "There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer."

column2: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
column6: Anointed to preach good tidings to the meek, bind up the brokenhearted, proclaim liberty to the captives. Jesus read this in the synagogue at Nazareth and said, "This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears."
Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh. Matthew joins this to Zechariah's words when Jesus rides into Jerusalem.
One comes in garments red from treading the winepress of God's wrath alone. Revelation shows Christ, in a vesture dipped in blood, treading the winepress of the wrath of God.

column2: The righteous Branch: The LORD our righteousness
column6: A righteous Branch raised up to David, a King who shall reign and prosper, whose name is THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS. Christ is made unto us righteousness.
Rachel weeping for her children refused to be comforted. Matthew says this was fulfilled when Herod killed the boys of Bethlehem, trying to kill the infant Jesus.
God promised a new covenant: his law written on the heart, and sins remembered no more. At the Last Supper Jesus said, "This cup is the new testament in my blood."
God will set up one shepherd over his flock, "my servant David", their prince for ever. Written long after David died: fulfilled in Jesus, the Son of David and the good shepherd.
A stone cut out without hands breaks the kingdoms of the world and becomes a mountain filling the earth: God's kingdom that shall never be destroyed. The kingdom of Christ.

column2: One like the Son of man
column6: One like the Son of man comes with the clouds of heaven and is given an everlasting kingdom. "Son of man" was Jesus' own name for himself, and he quoted this at his trial.

Seventy weeks to finish transgression, make reconciliation for iniquity and bring in everlasting righteousness; Messiah the Prince shall be cut off, but not for himself. Traditionally read of the time of Christ's coming and death.
After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up. Traditionally read of Christ, raised the third day "according to the scriptures".

column2: Out of Egypt have I called my son
column6: God called Israel, his son, out of Egypt. Matthew sees it fulfilled in Jesus, the true Son, brought back from Egypt as a child.

column2: O death, where is thy sting?
column6: I will ransom them from the power of the grave... O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction. Paul's song of Christ's victory over death.

column2: Whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD
column6: Whoever calls on the name of the LORD shall be delivered. Peter and Paul apply it to calling on the name of the Lord Jesus.
God will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, and the nations will be called by his name. James said this is fulfilled as Gentiles come to Christ.
As Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. Jesus' sign of his death and resurrection.

But thou, Bethlehem... out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting. The scribes told Herod the Christ would be born there.

column2: The Branch, priest upon his throne
column6: My servant the BRANCH shall build the temple of the LORD and be a priest upon his throne. Christ is both King and Priest, building God's temple, his people.

column2: Thy King cometh, riding upon an ass
column6: Behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass. Jesus rode into Jerusalem this way to fulfil it.
The shepherd was valued at thirty pieces of silver, cast to the potter in the house of the LORD. Judas was paid thirty pieces of silver; it went to buy the potter's field.

column2: They shall look upon me whom they have pierced
column6: They shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him. John saw the soldier pierce Jesus' side and wrote that this scripture was fulfilled.
Smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered. Jesus quoted it on the night of his arrest, and all the disciples fled.

column2: The Lord shall suddenly come to his temple
column6: God sends his messenger to prepare the way, and the Lord comes suddenly to his temple. Jesus said John was that messenger; Jesus himself came to the temple.
Unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings. Zacharias sang of Christ as the dayspring from on high.
Elijah will come before the great day of the LORD. Jesus said John the Baptist was the Elijah who was to come, going before the Lord Jesus.
In mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging. The angel told Mary her son would sit on David's throne.

column2: A king shall reign in righteousness
column6: A king reigns in righteousness, and a man is a hiding place from the wind and a shelter from the storm. Traditionally read of Christ, the righteous King who gives rest.
I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God. In Revelation the risen Jesus says the same of himself: "I am the first and the last."

column2: Called and named from the womb
column6: The servant was called from the womb and named before birth, despised by the nation, yet kings shall rise and worship. Jesus was named by the angel before he was born.
The servant speaks a word in season to the weary, his ear opened each morning; he sets his face like a flint. Jesus spoke only what the Father taught him and set his face to go to Jerusalem.
The Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising; they bring gold and incense. The wise men brought gold and frankincense to Jesus.
They shall serve the LORD their God, "and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them". Written long after David's death: fulfilled in Christ, the Son of David.

column2: Until he come whose right it is
column6: The crown is taken away and overturned "until he come whose right it is; and I will give it him". Traditionally read of Christ, the rightful King.

column2: The tender twig on the high mountain
column6: God takes a tender twig from the top of the cedar and plants it on a high mountain, and it becomes a goodly cedar sheltering every bird. Traditionally read of Christ, the shoot of David's line, and his kingdom.
The desire of all nations shall come: and I will fill this house with glory... The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former. Christ came to that temple.

column2: I will dwell in the midst of thee
column6: Lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD, and many nations shall join themselves to him. God came to dwell among us in Christ.
In that day there shall be a fountain opened... for sin and for uncleanness. Blood and water flowed from Jesus' side; his blood cleanses from all sin.

column2: His feet upon the mount of Olives
column6: His feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, and the LORD shall be king over all the earth. Jesus ascended from the mount of Olives, and the angels said he would come again in like manner.
